description: "The Clock-driven half of the promise feedback loop with order-management (ADR 0014 §5, this service's own ADR-0025): scans every task still open (Pending or Claimed — i.e. not Completed) and, for each whose CPT is at or before now, publishes `TaskCPTMissed`. Unlike `/tasks/expire-leases`, this never mutates the task's own lifecycle state — a CPT miss is a fact reported upstream, not a state transition. A collection-level action on the `tasks` resource, mirroring `/tasks/expire-leases`'s own convention exactly. **Not idempotent in the usual sense by design**: a task still open past its CPT is reported again on every sweep pass for as long as it remains open — order-management's `RepromiseOrder` consumer is explicitly designed (ADR 0014 §5) to be idempotent on `(orderId, sourceEventId)` because of this. Takes no request body."

The Clock-driven half of the promise feedback loop with order-management (ADR 0014 §5, this service's own ADR-0025): scans every task still open (Pending or Claimed — i.e. not Completed) and, for each whose CPT is at or before now, publishes `TaskCPTMissed`. Unlike `/tasks/expire-leases`, this never mutates the task's own lifecycle state — a CPT miss is a fact reported upstream, not a state transition. A collection-level action on the `tasks` resource, mirroring `/tasks/expire-leases`'s own convention exactly. **Not idempotent in the usual sense by design**: a task still open past its CPT is reported again on every sweep pass for as long as it remains open — order-management's `RepromiseOrder` consumer is explicitly designed (ADR 0014 §5) to be idempotent on `(orderId, sourceEventId)` because of this. Takes no request body.
